item.title: Year in Review: Mary Claire Wooten’s Top 5 stories of 2025
item.description: Alabama’s 2025 politics featured abortion access battles, civil legal aid threats, parole reform pressure, agency transparency fights and Doug Jones’s gubernatorial entry.

item.title: Prefiled bill details new eviction notice, grants immunity
item.description: Prefiled in December, the bill would require eviction notices to contain language about how landlords can handle tenants’ personal property.

item.title: Candice Duvieilh on managing growth, improving accountability in District 5
item.description: Candidate Candice Duvieilh emphasized her policy expertise and background in public administration, saying she was more qualified than the current representative.

item.title: Opinion | Radical common sense
item.description: Published into a crisis of conscience among colonists, Paine’s "Common Sense" supplied the organizing principle for independence 250 years ago.

item.title: Jefferson County Democratic Party opens candidate qualifying for 2026 primary
item.description: Party officials emphasized the importance of the three-week window, stating the process ensures leaders committed to good governance were elected.

item.title: Year in Review: Chance Phillips’ Top 5 stories of 2025
item.description: In 2025, Alabama politics was shaped by fights over “DEI,” changes to federal funding, and secrets kept by state politicians.

item.title: Alabama reacts to Trump’s surprise assault on Venezuela
item.description: Alabama lawmakers split sharply after the military action; Republicans praised the capture while Democrats condemned the strike as unconstitutional.

item.title: Women Voters to host training on use of The Alabama Channel
item.description: The Alabama Channel provides live streams and recordings of public meetings, offering citizens powerful tools for transparency and civic participation.

item.title: Opinion | What conservatism once meant—and what has replaced it today
item.description: Traditional conservatism valued restraint, character, and stable institutions. Today, a politics of conflict and resentment threatens the civic foundations of democracy.

item.title: Opinion | Operation Oily Epstein in Venezuela seems very, very familiar
item.description: Trump has gone around Congress to kidnap a foreign leader and take control of another country. We know how that ends.
